answer:
Use a finite-volume grid with Nx=400 uniform cells on the spatial domain [-1, 1].
Set dx=2/Nx=0.005 and cell centers x_j=-1+(j+0.5)*dx for j=0,...,399.
Set CFL=0.5 and final time T=0.5.
Set Gamma=1.6666666666666667, eta=0.1, zeta=eta=0.1.
Define m=rho*v and E=p/(Gamma-1)+0.5*rho*v^2.
Initialize cell-averaged conservative variables U=[rho,m,E] by evaluating the smooth initial conditions at the cell centers.
Use rho(x,0)=1.0+0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x,0)=0.1*cos(pi*x), and p(x,0)=1.0+0.2*cos(pi*x) with arguments in radians.
Recover the pressure from p=(Gamma-1)*(E-0.5*m^2/rho), clipping rho and p to a minimum of 1e-12 if needed.
Use the Rusanov numerical flux for the inviscid Euler part with interface wave speed a=max(|v_L|+c_L, |v_R|+c_R), where c=sqrt(Gamma*p/rho).
Compute v_x with a centered difference on the cell-centered v values.
Compute sigma=(zeta+4/3*eta)*v_x.
Approximate sigma at each interface by averaging neighboring cell-centered sigma values.
Add the viscous interface flux F_visc=[0,-sigma,-v*sigma] using interface-averaged v and sigma.
Use the total interface flux F_total=F_hat+F_visc.
Evolve the semi-discrete finite-volume system with two-stage SSP-RK2 (Heun's method).
Choose the time step each stage as dt=min(dt_conv, dt_visc), where dt_conv=CFL*dx/max_j(|v_j|+c_j) and dt_visc=0.5*dx^2/max(zeta+4/3*eta, 1e-30).
Adjust the final time step so that T=0.5 is hit exactly.
Implement periodic boundary conditions by wrapping ghost-cell indices.
At final time T, compute rho, v, and p on the cell centers.
Save the file solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz containing arrays x, rho, v, p and scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, CFL.
Save a three-panel line plot of rho, v, and p versus x at time T as solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png.
Print the min and max of rho and p as a positivity check.
Print the mean of rho over the spatial domain as a mass conservation check.
